faults.name: wstrb_wdata_swapped
faults.why: the write strobe is taken from the wrong bits of the packed word

faults.name: bresp_dropped
faults.why: the write response is replaced by OKAY

faults.name: rready_not_forwarded
faults.why: the read-data channel ignores the master's rready

faults.name: araddr_offset
faults.why: the read address is taken one bit off

faults.name: axi4_rlast_swapped
faults.why: rlast is taken from rresp

faults.name: axi4_awlen_dropped
faults.why: the burst length is forced to one beat

faults.name: credit_double_return
faults.why: a returned credit counts as two: the sender sends into a full receiver buffer

faults.name: ready_without_credit
faults.why: s_ready ignores the credit count: the sender sends with no credit and the receiver buffer overflows

faults.name: credit_lost_when_both
faults.why: a credit arriving in the clock a beat is sent is dropped: credits leak and the channel slows then stops

faults.name: credit_start_zero
faults.why: the sender starts with no credits: nothing is ever sent

faults.name: write_pointer_no_wrap
faults.why: the write pointer does not wrap at CREDITS: wrong entries for a depth that is not a power of two

faults.name: read_wrong_entry
faults.why: the output reads the write position, not the read position

faults.name: pop_without_ready
faults.why: the read pointer advances whenever the output is valid, not when it is taken: a stalled beat is skipped

faults.name: valid_one_clock_late
faults.why: m_valid follows the buffer count one clock late: a beat is offered after it was popped

faults.name: forward_stage_skips
faults.why: a forward stage takes its data from the first stage, not the previous one

faults.name: return_stage_drops
faults.why: a credit-return stage past the first drops every credit

faults.name: count_unaccepted_beat
faults.why: a beat that was offered but not accepted enters the channel

faults.name: buffer_write_ignores_valid
faults.why: the receiver buffer is written on every clock: an entry is overwritten by an invalid beat

faults.name: comb_ready_ignores_take
faults.why: the comb slice's s_ready no longer depends on m_ready: it works but at half throughput and with a different ready timing

faults.name: comb_reset_keeps_valid
faults.why: reset does not clear the comb slice's valid: a beat survives a reset

faults.name: half_ready_stale
faults.why: the half slice's ready register is computed from the old valid: it accepts a second beat into a full slice

faults.name: half_drop_unready
faults.why: the half slice empties itself without waiting for m_ready: a stalled beat is lost

faults.name: skid_ready_too_late
faults.why: the skid buffer stays ready one clock too long: the side register is overwritten

faults.name: skid_park_dropped
faults.why: the skid buffer never parks the beat that arrives after m_ready falls: it is lost

faults.name: skid_drain_wrong_source
faults.why: the side register drains into the output register from the wrong source: the parked beat is replaced by the input

faults.name: full_write_pointer_stuck
faults.why: the full slice's write pointer stops alternating: later beats overwrite the same entry

faults.name: full_read_swapped
faults.why: the full slice reads the entries in the wrong order: two beats swap

faults.name: full_ready_overfill
faults.why: the full slice never says not-ready: a third beat overwrites an unread one

faults.name: fwd_enable_needs_ready
faults.why: the shared enable ignores an empty output: a sink that waits for valid before ready never sees the beat

faults.name: fwd_first_stage_free_running
faults.why: the first stage's data register loads on every clock, not only when enabled: a stalled beat is overwritten

faults.name: chain_output_ready_ignored
faults.why: the last slice is told the sink is always ready: beats are lost while the sink stalls

faults.name: wire_ready_constant
faults.why: the N = 0 wire tells the source it is ready whatever the sink says

faults.name: fwd_valid_gated_by_ready
faults.why: the output's tvalid depends on tready (forbidden by AXI4-Stream): the bench's tready flip within a clock sees it; the port rules cannot, because a gated valid never looks withdrawn
